title: I Used the Community Coffee-Roaster Drum Log on the Chair Who Camped My Batch

parts.text: I stepped into roaster bay at 6:04 a.m. and chair Oren was already using my numbered green. The board said: ONE BATCH. FORTY MINUTES. DRUM STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-four, co-op lead, holding a clipboard that listed our roast. Oren shrugged. "Chairs keep the drum." I photographed the board, the booking, and his beans in my drum. Then I asked for the drum log. At 6:12 the co-op desk pinged why Oren's beans sat in our drum. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The co-op desk can see Oren's beans in the drum during our roast.

social.video_title: He camped my numbered roast batch — Part 1/2
social.description: Community roaster, a chair in my drum, a forty-minute clock he posted. I logged the beans. Would you have asked for the drum log?

parts.text: Oren called it sample roasts until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the drum still. The green went back to my numbered bin. Oren ran a slot of their own and told the next chair atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: CHAIRS DO NOT KEEP THE DRUM. I keep our roast on a labeled card. Oren brown-bags his samples. The drum finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Chairs do not keep the drum — Part 2/2
social.description: Drum log, numbered green, and a second line on the board. Were sample roasts ever our batch?
